50526246.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant human Keap1 Kelch domain (321 to 609 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)pLysS by SPR-based solution competition assay
50526246.references_previous: Reference 59: Hu, L.; Magesh, S.; Beamer, L. J.; Wang, L.; Lewis, T. A.; Chen, Y.; Khodier, J. E.; Inoyama, D.; Beamer, L. J.; Emge, T. J.; Shen, J.; Kerrigan, J. E.; Kong, A. N.; Dandapani, S.; Palmer, M.; Schreiber, S. L.; Munoz, B. Discovery of a Small-Molecule Inhibitor and Cellular Probe of Keap1–Nrf2 Protein-Protein Interaction. Bioorg. Med. Chem. Lett. 2013, 23, 3039–3043.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: The SPR-based solution competition assay was performed as described previously. Briefly, recombinant human Keap1 Kelch domain (321 to 609 residues) was expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)pLysS and purified as described previously. The purified protein was immobilized on a CM5 sensor chip (GE Healthcare) via amine coupling. The binding of the Nrf2 ETGE peptide to Keap1 was monitored in real time. The dissociation rate constant (koff) was determined from the dissociation phase of the sensorgram. The association rate constant (kon) was determined from the association phase of the sensorgram. The equilibrium dissociation constant (KD) was calculated as KD = koff/kon. The SPR-based solution competition assay was performed by pre-incubating the Nrf2 ETGE peptide with the test compound for 10 min at room temperature before injection onto the sensor chip. The concentration of the Nrf2 ETGE peptide was 100 nM. The test compound was added at various concentrations (0, 1, 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 1000 nM). The buffer used was HEPES (10 mM, pH 7.4) containing 150 mM NaCl, 0.05% Tween 20, and 0.01% BSA. The flow rate was 30 μL/min. The temperature was 25°C. The data were analyzed using BIAevaluation software (GE Healthcare).
original_paragraph.Figure 5 caption: Figure 5. Discovery and optimization of Keap1–Nrf2 inhibitors with a THIQ (tetrahydroisoquinoline) scaffold. (A) The development process of the Keap1–Nrf2 inhibitors with THIQ scaffold. (B) The binding mode differences between the hit and optimal compounds. Key modifications are labeled with yellow dashed lines. Hydrogen bonds are represented by green dashed lines, and electrostatic interactions are represented by yellow dashed lines. The carbon atoms of small molecules and Keap1 residues are colored cyan and purple, respectively. Key water molecules are represented by red dots.
